title: Matched Data, Better Models: Target Aligned Data Filtering with Sparse Autoencoders
claim: Per-sample quality scores discard low-scoring samples that carry unique concepts, so individual scoring misses useful data.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, image above caption with colored score text
description: A single rounded gray box holds three photographs in a row, each captioned with a quoted text and a CLIP-Score percentile. On the left is three kittens in front of a bright green blurred background, captioned "Green background" with red text "CLIP-Score: bottom 5%". In the center is a side-view tabby cat looking upward against a dark background, captioned "Cat" with blue text "CLIP-Score: top 20%". On the right is a gray cat with yellow eyes, captioned "Yellow eyed cat" with blue text "CLIP-Score: top 20%". The red versus blue coloring draws the eye first to the low-scoring left image. It shows that a filter keeping only top-scoring samples would drop the only example of the concept green.
caption: Quality Score Limitations. Low-quality samples can still be useful for learning broader concepts. For example, a model may have enough samples to learn the concept of “cat,” but without the low-scoring “green background” image, it lacks examples needed to learn the concept of “green.”
abstract: Data filtering plays a central role in improving model performance, particularly for vision language models that are pretrained on large, noisy, and redundant image-caption datasets. Existing filtering techniques assess every sample individually and retain those that exceed a certain quality threshold, but such strategies fail to capture higher-order interactions. In this work, we propose a novel submodular framework for data selection that addresses this limitation. Our method, Submodular Distribution Matching (SDM), selects a subset by: (1) training a type of sparse autoencoder to learn disentangled and \emph{monotone} features; (2) estimating a target feature distribution from a target dataset; and (3) selecting a subset of samples whose feature distribution closely matches the target via submodular maximization. Given the DataComp-medium training set and no external models, SDM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on both ImageNet-1K and average performance across 38 downstream tasks. On the full DataComp-medium benchmark, SDM delivers performance within 1\% of the state-of-the-art results while using over \textbf{\emph{5×}} fewer GPU hours than the leading approach.
